# UtcOffset

A fixed shift from UTC, in whole minutes.

```rux
pub struct UtcOffset {
    pub seconds: int32;
}
```

Fixed is the word doing the work: this names what an offset is at one moment, and never which zone produced it
or when that zone changes its mind. Zone rules are a database with a release cycle, and belong to a later phase.

## Fields

| Name      | Type    | Description                                                               |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seconds` | `int32` | The shift in seconds east of UTC, negative west, within a day either way. |

## Associated functions

<h3 id="utc"><code>Utc</code></h3>

```rux

```

UTC itself.

**Returns**: the zero offset

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L197)

<h3 id="of"><code>Of</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Of(hours: int32, minutes: int32) -> UtcOffset?
```

The offset `hours` and `minutes` from UTC, when it is one an offset can be.
The two carry the same sign — minus five thirty is `Of(-5, -30)` — and the whole must stay within a day.
Real offsets stop at eighteen hours, but text may carry any legal-looking one and refusing to represent it
would turn parsing into policy.

| Name      | Type    | Description      |
| --------- | ------- | ---------------- |
| `hours`   | `int32` | how many hours   |
| `minutes` | `int32` | how many minutes |

**Returns**: the offset, or `None` when it is outside the range UTC offsets take

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L209)

## Implements Display

`UtcOffset` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    self: &UtcOffset,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the offset as `Z` for UTC, and as a signed `+HH:MM` otherwise.
`Z` rather than `+00:00` because that is what RFC 3339 names UTC, and because the two are the same offset
written two ways rather than two different offsets. A value that must be `+00:00` in its output is not
asking about the offset but about the format, which is a question for whatever assembles the text.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for a style other than `iso8601` or
`rfc3339`, or for a precision, which an offset has nothing to apply one to.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole offset was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L221)
